**Analysis:**
- Test image: Dark brown-to-black discoloration on cauliflower curd, localized patches, no mushy/wet appearance
- Black Rot (Xanthomonas campestris) is well-known to cause blackening of vascular tissue that extends into the curd
- Bacterial Soft Rot would typically present as water-soaked, mushy, collapsing tissue - not visible here
- Alternaria Leaf Spot and Downy Mildew affect leaves, not curds primarily
- The dry, firm-looking dark patches on the curd are characteristic of Black Rot advancing into the head

The curd blackening pattern strongly aligns with Black Rot, where vascular infection discolors and darkens the cauliflower head tissue.
